steps.content: Through the glass flap on the door, you see the young girl in the interrogation room.
She sits there quietly without the slightest hint of warmth in her eyes.

You feel the thick protective suit on you, and glance at the myriad of surveillance devices in the interrogation room. After confirming that it's safe, you push the door open and switch on the lights.
Hi, Pacassi.
Pacassi lifts her head slightly, on which is her pale, apathetic face.
MBCC and the Ring Research Institute have reached an agreement to transfer you here. You will live here as a Sinner detained by MBCC from now on.
Of course, given that you will be living in the Bureau from now on, I'll have to confirm some important security matters with you.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I understand.
Pacassi's voice is cold and distant.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Please start the interrogation.

You glance at the nuclear detection module on the wall. The old device, provided by the Ring Research Institute, is almost static. The numbers on the screen fluctuate between 0.3 and 0.5—which means you're safe, for now.
You pick up the files in your hand and unwrap the bag labeled with a nuclear radiation warning sign, thinking about your conversation with Nightingale earlier today.
Nightingale frowns next to the desk. When she sees you coming in, she puts down the file in her hand and stands up with a stern face.
Since the Ring Research Institute transferred Pacassi over, MBCC has been preparing for Pacassi's detainment, while Nightingale sorts out some relevant information.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Below are the original descriptions.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: "Although the subject has shown no intent to attack, radiation levels continue to accumulate when she stays in one place for a long time."

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: "When the subject experiences emotional fluctuations, the radiation level increases abnormally and can reach up to 1986.4 Roentgen."

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: "Tissue cut from the subject continues to emit intense radiation, and decontamination is extremely costly."
She's not a Sinner from the DisCity, is she? How does she have such a dangerous ability?
Nightingale shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: It's not specified in the file. It is only known that eight years ago, an unusual energy reaction was detected somewhere 2,000 kilometers north of the DisCity, where the Ring Research Institute monitored.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Documents show that an abandoned nuclear power plant was located there.
A nuclear power plant?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: It's an energy facility in the olden days. It used technology destroyed and eliminated by the city-states—which had devastating power too.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...When the rescue team arrived, the human settlement, Mayek, was already leveled to the ground. Pacassi was the only survivor.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Some researchers suspected that Pacassi was responsible for the nuclear accident, but there was no evidence.
And they never asked Pacassi about it?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: There's no relevant information. The Research Institute didn't have a professional interrogation department after all, and they would't do anything beyond their duties.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: In fact, they only studied Pacassi's abilities for the first couple of years. For the few years after that, Pacassi had been locked in a radiation isolation room.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The Research Institute didn't care about this Sinner who had lost her research value, nor was it obligated to find out the truth behind the incident in Mayek.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: They just dismissed Pacassi as a nuisance and sent her to the Bureau.
Now, this "nuisance," the suspect behind Mayek's destruction, is sitting before you.
You waste no time, flipping through the file Nightingale has summarized for you, and formally begin the interrogation.

Tell me about your ability.
Pacassi looks at you in the eyes and replies,

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: A radiation field with a maximum radius of about 100 meters and a maximum level of about 2,000 Roentgen.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: It can be activated by will, or reactively released by external triggers.
Looks like you know your ability very well.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I just memorized what they said in their research.
Her voice sounds calm while her body remains unmoved.
How are you feeling?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Great.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I don't need to eat or rest. My strength and endurance have improved a lot. And the radiation doesn't affect me.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I feel great.
Pacassi shakes her head while her eyes subconsciously glance at her mechanical arm.
Does your arm hurt?
The dark metal sheen of the paint looks out of place on the young girl.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: ...Okay.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: The nerves connected to the prosthesis can hurt.
Did the Ring Research Institute install the prosthesis for you?
You are a little curious. After all, it isn't very common to see such exquisite bionic device, even in the DisCity.
If Pacassi had lost her arm in a small remote town before gaining the Sinner's ability, it would have been a massive inconvenience in her life.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: They added the bionic fibers, but the metal structure inside was installed in the town.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: It's been too long. The nerves were already connected to it, so it couldn't be replaced anymore.
Did it happen before the explos... before you became a Sinner?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Yes.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: It was an accident in a pipe repair.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I got used to the prosthesis very quickly. The pain was tolerable, and it didn't affect work.
You had to work after you lost your arm? What did you do?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Same as before.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Check and repair the pipes of the nuclear power plant three times a week, weed the fields, and help the mayor process and deliver documents.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: That's all.
That's too much work for a child.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Chief.
Pacassi stares into your eyes, her voice clearly sounding more emotional.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: The DisCity is different from us and most places in the world.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: The DisCity has abundant energy and Hypercubes to avoid natural disasters.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: But Mayek didn't... We couldn't afford to feed idlers.
...I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I didn't mean to blame you.
I know, but I must apologize.
Pacassi speaks no more. The atmosphere becomes peaceful again.
Only then do you realize that not once did the device on the wall send out an alarm during the whole process of questioning just now.
This isn't quite consistent with what the Ring Research Institute claimed.

You lay out more documents before Pacassi, and a few of the images look particularly appalling.
Large, ruined steel and concrete buildings, piles of shattered concrete blocks and debris, and a crumbling ghost town covered with vines...
This is Mayek, Pacassi's hometown. Or rather, the ruins of her hometown.
Pacassi, there's an important issue I must figure out in this interrogation.
The truth behind Mayek's destruction.
Pacassi lowers her head.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: It was an accident.

options: Was it planned? Or was it a mere accident?

choices.text: Was it planned? Or was it a mere accident?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Both.
Can you elaborate more?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: ...The nuclear power plant in Mayek had been close to its limits for as long as I could remember.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: We were struggling to keep it running, but there's no way we could stop it from deteriorating and becoming more dangerous.
Was there no other solution?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Mayek was in this continent's northernmost part. Half of the year was winter.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: There was no way we could survive without the energy generated from the nuclear power plant.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Many did, including my parents.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: They went to the south, to the city of dreams where they didn't have to worry about the cold and hunger... They abandoned us.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: But there were always people who wanted to stay.
Pacassi raises her head.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: We knew about the nuclear war that destroyed half the world after Nightfall and the risk of accidents with nuclear power plants.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: But we had no choice if we wanted to survive in our hometown.
But still, your town...

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Fewer and fewer people stayed. Eventually, we didn't even have enough staff to operate the power plant.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: There was more and more work on everyone's shoulders. A lot of them couldn't take it anymore.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Before the accident, there were only two people left in the town.
You and the mayor, Longyear?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Yes.
You said Mayek's destruction wasn't entirely a pure accident.
If it wasn't you, was it Longyear the mayor?
Pacassi looks slightly stunned.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: No... He just...

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: It was my fault.
The fact that Pacassi tries to hide it makes you more certain of your speculation.

In the early years of Nightfall, a nuclear war lasting for years wiped out most of human civilization. The survivors signed the Nuclear Restriction Pact, which banned all nuclear technology, including nuclear power plants.
You should know the implications of this pact, Pacassi.
Pacassi purses her lips without giving a response.
All I want is the truth, a reason for you to stay in the Bureau without being feared...
Whatever you've gone through in Mayek is all in the past. Mayek doesn't exist anymore. There's nothing more for you to protect.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: That's not true!
Pacassi suddenly raises her voice.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I'm still alive. Mayek hasn't disappeared!

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: It's Longyear's life. It's our home... They were the ones who took me in when I was abandoned...

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Yet I couldn't save him...
Pacassi looks up, her eyes full of tears.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I deserted him. I deserted Mayek...
Pacassi lowers her head after finishing the words in trembles. With her going through such emotional turmoil, you subconsciously glance at the surveillance device on the wall.
To your surprise, the numbers on the device are as calm as a late autumn lake.
Looking at the young girl weeping in front of you, you can't help but reaching out.
Pacassi...
Don't worry. The Bureau is your new shelter. We won't abandon you, and we won't use you for experiments...
You can consider it your... home, if you will.
You try to comfort her, yet your words seem so empty.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I don't have a home anymore. Not since that winter when Mayek and Longyear was gone.
Pacassi's voice is cold and resisting.
Looking at the grieving young girl before you, you realize any words of comfort are simply pointless right now.
Perhaps you should leave her alone for now.
